title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 108 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 556–558 (Night 108, continuing directly from nights-107), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 108 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. Sulaymān Shāh's vizier stands before King Zahrshāh of the White Land and recites a poem that turns from the language of love into the king's praise. When the court has eaten and withdrawn, he asks for Zahrshāh's daughter in marriage for his master. Zahrshāh rises and kisses the ground, calls himself Sulaymān Shāh's subject, and has the marriage contracted at once by proxy before judges and witnesses. Two months of feasting follow; the princess is sent off in a golden litter with her slave girls and treasures, Zahrshāh rides three parasangs with the train, and the vizier sets out for home with the bride. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ الثَّامِنَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-thāminatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the eighth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and eighth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ وَزِيرَ الْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ لَمَّا دَخَلَ عَلَى الْمَلِكِ زَهْرْشَاه ثَبَّتَ جَنَانَهُ وَأَطْلَقَ لِسَانَهُ وَأَبْدَى فَصَاحَةَ الْوُزَرَاءِ وَتَكَلَّمَ بِكَلَامِ الْبُلَغَاءِ وَأَشَارَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ بِلُطْفِ الْتِفَاتٍ وَأَنْشَدَ هَذِهِ الْأَبْيَاتَ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna wazīra al-maliki sulaymāna shāh lammā dakhala ʿalā al-maliki zahrshāh thabbata janānahu wa-aṭlaqa lisānahu wa-abdā faṣāḥata al-wuzarāʾi wa-takallama bi-kalāmi al-bulaghāʾi wa-ashāra ilā al-maliki bi-luṭfi iltifātin wa-anshada hādhihi al-abyāta
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier of King Sulaymān Shāh, when he entered upon King Zahrshāh, made-firm his heart and let-loose his tongue, and showed the eloquence of viziers, and spoke with the speech of the eloquent, and gestured to the king with a grace of turning, and recited these verses:
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that when the vizier of King Sulaymān Shāh came in before King Zahrshāh, he steadied his heart and loosed his tongue, and with all a vizier's eloquence he spoke as the masters of speech speak; then, turning gracefully toward the king, he recited these verses:
sentences.n: Shahrazād takes up the night by repeating the scene that closed the last one. bi-, “with”: the manner of the gesture; iltifāt is a turning of the head or body toward someone.

sentences.t:
وَافَى وَاَقْبَلَ فِي الْغَلَائِلِ يَنْثَنِي * يُولِي الْهُدَى لِلْمُجْتَنَى وَالْمُجْتَنِي
وَرَقَى فَمَا تُغْنِى التَّمَائِمُ وَالرُّقَا * وَالسِّحْرُ مِنْ لَحَظَاتِ تِلْكَ الْاَعْيُنِ
قُلْ لِلْعَوَاذِلِ لَاتَلُومُوا اِنَّنِي * طُولَ الْمُدَى عَنْ حُبِّهِ لَا انْثَنِي
حَتَّى فُؤَادِي خَانَنِي وَوَفَى لَهُ * وَكَذَا الرُّقَادُ صَبَا اِلَيْهِ وَمَلَّنِي
يَاقَلْبُ مَا اَمْسَيْتَ وَحْدَكَ رَافَةً * فَامْكُثْ لَدَيْهِ وَاِنْ تَكُنْ اَوْحَشْتَنِي
لَا شَىْءَ يُطْرِبُ مَسْمَعِي بِسَمَاعِهِ * اِلَّا الثَّنَاءُ لِزَهْرِشَاهِ اَجْتَنِي
مَلِكٌ اِذَا اَنْفَقْتَ عُمْرَكَ كُلَّهُ * فِي نَظْرَةٍ مِنْ وَجْهِهِ اَنْتَ الْغَنِي
وَاِذَا انْتَخَبْتَ لَهُ دُعَاءً صَالِحًا * لَمْ تَلْقَ غَيْرَ مُشَارِكٍ وَمُؤَمِّنِ
يَااَهْلَ ذَا الْمُلْكِ الَّذِي مَنْ فَاتَهُ * وَرَجَا سِوَاهُ فَمَا اَرَاهُ بِمُؤْمِنِ
sentences.tr:
wāfā wa-aqbala fī al-ghalāʾili yanthanī * yūlī al-hudā li-al-mujtanā wa-al-mujtanī
wa-raqā fa-mā tughnī al-tamāʾimu wa-al-ruqā * wa-al-siḥru min laḥaẓāti tilka al-aʿyuni
qul li-al-ʿawādhili lā talūmū innanī * ṭūla al-mudā ʿan ḥubbihi lā anthanī
ḥattā fuʾādī khānanī wa-wafā lahu * wa-ka-dhā al-ruqādu ṣabā ilayhi wa-mallanī
yā qalbu mā amsayta waḥdaka rāfatan * fa-umkuth ladayhi wa-in takun awḥashtanī
lā shayʾa yuṭribu masmaʿī bi-samāʿihi * illā al-thanāʾu li-zahrishāhi ajtanī
malikun idhā anfaqta ʿumraka kullahu * fī naẓratin min wajhihi anta al-ghanī
wa-idhā intakhabta lahu duʿāʾan ṣāliḥan * lam talqa ghayra mushārikin wa-muʾammini
yā ahla dhā al-mulki alladhī man fātahu * wa-rajā siwāhu fa-mā arāhu bi-muʾmini
sentences.l:
He came and drew-near in the fine-robes, swaying; he grants the guidance to the plucked and the plucker.
And he cast-spells, so the amulets and the charms avail nothing — and the magic (is) from the glances of those eyes.
Say to the blaming-women: Do not blame! I, the length of the span, from his love will not turn-back.
Even my heart betrayed me and kept-faith with him; and likewise the sleep inclined to him and wearied of me.
O heart, you did not pass-the-evening alone (in) pity; so stay with him, even if you have made-me-desolate.
No thing delights my hearing with its hearing except the praise of Zahrshāh, (which) I gather.
A king: if you spent your life, all of it, on a look at his face, you (would be) the rich one.
And if you chose for him a prayer good, you would not meet other than a sharer and one-who-says-amen.
O people of / worthy of this kingship — whoever misses him and hopes (in) other than him, I do not see him (as) a believer.
sentences.i:
He came, he drew near in his fine robes, swaying, and gave guidance to the one gathered and the one who gathers.
He cast his spell, and amulets and charms are of no avail: the magic lies in the glances of those eyes.
Tell the women who blame me: blame me not; for all time to come I will not turn from loving him.
Even my heart betrayed me and kept faith with him; and sleep, too, went over to him and grew weary of me.
O heart, it was not out of pity that you spent the evening alone; stay with him, then, though you leave me desolate.
Nothing delights my ear to hear but the praise of Zahrshāh, which I gather in.
A king: if you spent your whole life on a single look at his face, you would be the rich one.
And if you chose a good prayer for him, you would find no one who did not join in it and say amen.
O you who are worthy of this kingship: whoever passes him by and sets his hopes on another, I do not count him a believer.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the print points it. The poem begins in the language of love and turns, in its sixth line, into praise of Zahrshāh; the beloved of the opening lines may already be the king, as courtly panegyric often has it. The first line is obscure: al-mujtanā and al-mujtanī are “the one plucked” and “the one who plucks”, chosen for the rhyme, and al-hudā, “guidance”, gives no easy sense with them (perhaps a misprint for al-hawā, “love”); it is translated only as far as the words allow. rāfatan in the fifth line is raʾfa, “pity, tenderness”, with the hamza unwritten; the line's sense is uncertain. The print points al-mudā in the third line, literally “knives”; the sense wants madā, “span”, and it is translated so. Zahrshāh's name is pointed zahri-shāh in the sixth line, for the metre. yā ahla dhā al-mulki in the last line may be “O people of this realm” or “O you worthy of this kingship”; the second is translated. The rhyme is on -ni/-nī.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا فَرَغَ الْوَزِيرُ مِنْ هَذَا النِّظَامِ قَرَّبَهُ الْمَلِكُ زَهْرْشَاه وَأَكْرَمَهُ غَايَةَ الْإِكْرَامِ وَأَجْلَسَهُ بِجَانِبِهِ وَتَبَسَّمَ فِي وَجْهِهِ وَشَرَّفَهُ بِلَطِيفِ الْكَلَامِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā faragha al-wazīru min hādhā al-niẓāmi qarrabahu al-maliku zahrshāh wa-akramahu ghāyata al-ikrāmi wa-ajlasahu bi-jānibihi wa-tabassama fī wajhihi wa-sharrafahu bi-laṭīfi al-kalāmi
sentences.l: And when the vizier finished from this arrangement, King Zahrshāh brought him near and honoured him the utmost of honouring, and seated him at his side, and smiled in his face, and honoured him with gentle speech.
sentences.i: When the vizier had finished his poem, King Zahrshāh drew him close and showed him every possible honour; he seated him at his side, smiled on him, and honoured him with gracious words.
sentences.n: niẓām, “arrangement, stringing”, is verse, words strung like pearls. bi-, “at” in bi-jānibihi, “at his side”; “with” in bi-laṭīfi al-kalām. Rhymed: al-ikrām / al-kalām.

sentences.t: وَلَمْ يَزَالُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ إِلَى وَقْتِ الصَّبَاحِ ثُمَّ قَدَّمُوا السِّمَاطَ فِي ذَلِكَ الْإِيوَانِ فَأَكَلُوا جَمِيعًا حَتَّى اكْتَفَوْا ثُمَّ رَفَعُوا السِّمَاطَ وَخَرَجَ كُلُّ مَنْ فِى الْمَجْلِسِ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ إِلَّا الْخَوَاصُّ
sentences.tr: wa-lam yazālū ʿalā dhālika ilā waqti al-ṣabāḥi thumma qaddamū al-simāṭa fī dhālika al-īwāni fa-akalū jamīʿan ḥattā iktafaw thumma rafaʿū al-simāṭa wa-kharaja kullu man fī al-majlisi wa-lam yabqa illā al-khawāṣṣu
sentences.l: And they did not cease upon that until the time of the morning; then they set-forth the cloth in that hall, and they ate all-together until they had enough; then they lifted the cloth, and everyone who (was) in the assembly went out, and there did not remain except the intimates.
sentences.i: So they continued until morning. Then the table was spread in that hall, and they all ate their fill; the table was cleared, everyone in the assembly withdrew, and only the king's intimates remained.
sentences.n: simāṭ is the long cloth spread on the floor for a meal. The khawāṣṣ are the king's inner circle.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا رَأَى الْوَزِيرُ خُلُوَّ الْمَكَانِ نَهَضَ قَائِمًا عَلَى قَدَمَيْهِ وَأَثْنَى عَلَى الْمَلِكِ وَقَبَّلَ الْأَرْضَ بَيْنَ يَدَيْهِ ثُمَّ قَالَ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā raʾā al-wazīru khuluwwa al-makāni nahaḍa qāʾiman ʿalā qadamayhi wa-athnā ʿalā al-maliki wa-qabbala al-arḍa bayna yadayhi thumma qāla
sentences.l: And when the vizier saw the emptiness of the place, he rose standing on his two feet, and praised the king, and kissed the ground between his two hands; then he said:
sentences.i: When the vizier saw that the room had emptied, he rose to his feet, praised the king and kissed the ground before him, and said:
sentences.n: The print has قئما, a misprint for قائما, corrected here.

sentences.t: أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالسَّيِّدُ الْخَطِيرُ إِنِّي سَعَيْتُ إِلَيْكَ وَقَدِمْتُ عَلَيْكَ فِي أَمْرٍ لَكَ فِيهِ الصَّلَاحُ وَالْخَيْرُ وَالْفَلَاحُ
sentences.tr: ayyuhā al-maliku al-kabīru wa-al-sayyidu al-khaṭīru innī saʿaytu ilayka wa-qadimtu ʿalayka fī amrin laka fīhi al-ṣalāḥu wa-al-khayru wa-al-falāḥu
sentences.l: O king the great and lord the momentous, I have hastened to you and come upon you in a matter (that) for you in it (is) the good-order and the good and the prospering.
sentences.i: O great king and eminent lord, I have hastened to you and come before you on a matter that holds for you welfare, good and prosperity.
sentences.n: Rhymed pairs: al-kabīr / al-khaṭīr, ilayka / ʿalayka, al-ṣalāḥ / al-falāḥ.

sentences.t: وَهُوَ أَنِّي قَدْ أَتَيْتُكَ رَسُولًا خَاطِبًا وَفِي بِنْتِكَ الْحَسِيبَةِ النَّسِيبَةِ رَاغِبًا مِنْ عِنْدِ الْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ صَاحِبِ الْعَدْلِ وَالْأَمَانِ وَالْفَضْلِ وَالْإِحْسَانِ مَلِكِ الْأَرْضِ الْخَضْرَاءِ وَجِبَالِ أَصْفَهَانَ
sentences.tr: wa-huwa annī qad ataytuka rasūlan khāṭiban wa-fī bintika al-ḥasībati al-nasībati rāghiban min ʿindi al-maliki sulaymāna shāh ṣāḥibi al-ʿadli wa-al-amāni wa-al-faḍli wa-al-iḥsāni maliki al-arḍi al-khaḍrāʾi wa-jibāli aṣfahāna
sentences.l: And it (is) that I have come to you, a messenger asking-in-marriage, and in your daughter, the noble-born, the well-descended, desiring, from the presence of King Sulaymān Shāh, master of the justice and the safety, and the bounty and the beneficence, king of the Green Land and the mountains of Iṣfahān.
sentences.i: It is this: I have come to you as an envoy, seeking in marriage your noble, well-born daughter on behalf of King Sulaymān Shāh, lord of justice and safety, of bounty and kindness, king of the Green Land and the mountains of Iṣfahān.
sentences.n: The print has اتينك, a misprint for اتيتك, corrected here: the vizier speaks as “I” (annī). Rhymed: khāṭiban / rāghiban; al-amān / al-iḥsān / aṣfahān.

sentences.t: وَقَدْ أَرْسَلَ إِلَيْكَ الْهَدَايَا الْكَثِيرَةَ وَالتُّحَفَ الْغَزِيرَةَ وَهُوَ فِي مُصَاهَرَتِكَ رَاغِبٌ فَهَلْ أَنْتَ لَهُ كَذَلِكَ طَالِبٌ
sentences.tr: wa-qad arsala ilayka al-hadāyā al-kathīrata wa-al-tuḥafa al-ghazīrata wa-huwa fī muṣāharatika rāghibun fa-hal anta lahu ka-dhālika ṭālibun
sentences.l: And he has sent to you the gifts many and the rarities abundant, and he in marriage-alliance-with-you (is) desiring; so are you for him likewise seeking?
sentences.i: He has sent you many gifts and a wealth of rare things, and he desires to be joined to you by marriage; do you wish for the same with him?
sentences.n: muṣāhara is alliance by marriage, becoming someone's in-law. ka-, “like”: ka-dhālika, “like that, likewise”. Rhymed: al-kathīra / al-ghazīra, rāghib / ṭālib.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ سَكَتَ يَنْتَظِرُ الْجَوَابَ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu sakata yantaẓiru al-jawāba
sentences.l: Then he fell silent, awaiting the answer.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ زَهْرْ شَاه ذَلِكَ الْكَلَامَ نَهَضَ قَائِمًا عَلَى الْأَقْدَامِ وَلَثَمَ الْأَرْضَ بِاسْتِنَامٍ فَتَعَجَّبَ الْحَاضِرُونَ مِنْ خُضُوعِ الْمَلِكِ لِلرَّسُولِ وَانْدَهَشَتْ مِنْهُمُ الْعُقُولُ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku zahrshāh dhālika al-kalāma nahaḍa qāʾiman ʿalā al-aqdāmi wa-lathama al-arḍa bi-istināmin fa-taʿajjaba al-ḥāḍirūna min khuḍūʿi al-maliki li-al-rasūli wa-indahashat minhumu al-ʿuqūlu
sentences.l: And when King Zahrshāh heard that speech, he rose standing on the feet and kissed the ground with istinām; and those present marvelled at the submission of the king to the messenger, and the minds of them were astounded.
sentences.i: When King Zahrshāh heard these words he rose to his feet and kissed the ground in homage. Those present marvelled to see the king humble himself before the envoy, and their minds were struck with wonder.
sentences.n: The print splits the king's name, زهر شاه, as it does several times below. bi-istinām is obscure: istināma means to rely on someone or be at ease with him, which hardly fits. It may be a misprint for bi-istilām, kissing in reverence (the word used for touching and kissing the Black Stone), but that is a guess, so the print is kept and translated by the evident sense. li-, “to, before”: the king humbles himself to the envoy. Rhymed: al-aqdām / istinām, al-rasūl / al-ʿuqūl.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَثْنَي عَلَى ذِى الْجَلَالِ وَالْإِكْرَامِ وَقَالَ وَهُوَ فِي حَالَةِ الْقِيَامِ أَيُّهَا الْوَزِيرُ الْمُعَظَّمُ وَالسَّيِّدُ الْمُكَرَّمُ اسْمَعْ مَا أَقُولُ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika athnā ʿalā dhī al-jalāli wa-al-ikrāmi wa-qāla wa-huwa fī ḥālati al-qiyāmi ayyuhā al-wazīru al-muʿaẓẓamu wa-al-sayyidu al-mukarramu ismaʿ mā aqūlu
sentences.l: Then the king praised the Possessor of the Majesty and the Honour, and said, and he (was) in the state of the standing: O vizier the magnified and lord the honoured, hear what I say:
sentences.i: Then the king gave praise to God, Lord of Majesty and Honour, and said, still standing: O mighty vizier and honoured lord, hear what I say.
sentences.n: Dhū al-jalāl wa-al-ikrām, “Possessor of Majesty and Honour”, is a Qurʾānic name of God (Sūrat al-Raḥmān 55:27). athnā is printed with a dotted ي (اثني) for the usual ى.

sentences.t: إِنَّنَا لِلْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ رَعَايَاهُ وَنَتَشَرَّفُ بِنَسَبِهِ وَنُنَافِسُ فِيهِ وَابْنَتِي جَارِيَةٌ مِنْ جُمْلَةِ جَوَارِيهِ وَهَذَا أَجَلُّ مُرَادِي لِيَكُونَ ذُخْرِي وَاعْتِمَادِي
sentences.tr: innanā li-al-maliki sulaymāna shāh min jumlati raʿāyāhu wa-natasharrafu bi-nasabihi wa-nunāfisu fīhi wa-ibnatī jāriyatun min jumlati jawārīhi wa-hādhā ajallu murādī li-yakūna dhukhrī wa-iʿtimādī
sentences.l: We, to King Sulaymān Shāh, (are) among the whole of his subjects, and we are honoured by kinship-with-him and vie-for it; and my daughter (is) a slave-girl among the whole of his slave-girls; and this (is) the most-exalted of my desire, that it may be my treasure and my support.
sentences.i: We are King Sulaymān Shāh's subjects, one among the many; kinship with him is an honour, and one we would compete for. My daughter is but one slave girl among all his slave girls. This is the dearest of my wishes, to be my treasure and my stay.
sentences.n: li-, “to, of”: li-al-maliki ties “his subjects” to the king. bi-, “by”: natasharrafu bi-, “be honoured by”. nāfasa fī is to vie for a thing. Zahrshāh speaks of his daughter as a slave girl out of courtly humility. Rhymed: raʿāyāhu / jawārīhi, murādī / iʿtimādī.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّهُ أَحْضَرَ الْقُضَاةَ وَالشُّهُودَ وَشَهِدُوا أَنَّ الْمَلِكَ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ وَكَّلَ وَزِيرَهُ فِى الزَّوَاجِ وَتَوَلَّى الْمَلِكُ زَهْرْ شَاه عَقْدَ بِنْتِهِ بِابْتِهَاجٍ
sentences.tr: thumma innahu aḥḍara al-quḍāta wa-al-shuhūda wa-shahidū anna al-malika sulaymāna shāh wakkala wazīrahu fī al-zawāji wa-tawallā al-maliku zahrshāh ʿaqda bintihi bi-ibtihājin
sentences.l: Then he brought the judges and the witnesses, and they witnessed that King Sulaymān Shāh had made-agent his vizier in the marriage, and King Zahrshāh took-charge-of the contract of his daughter with joy.
sentences.i: Then he summoned the judges and witnesses, and they attested that King Sulaymān Shāh had appointed his vizier as his proxy for the marriage; and King Zahrshāh, rejoicing, gave his daughter in marriage himself.
sentences.n: The groom is married by proxy: his vizier stands for him, and the bride's father, as her guardian, concludes the contract (ʿaqd) on her behalf. bi-, “with”: bi-ibtihāj, “joyfully”. Rhymed: al-zawāj / ibtihāj.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْقُضَاةَ أَحْكَمُوا عَقْدَ النِّكَاحِ وَدَعَوْا لَهُمَا بِالْفَوْزِ وَالنَّجَاحِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-quḍāta aḥkamū ʿaqda al-nikāḥi wa-daʿaw lahumā bi-al-fawzi wa-al-najāḥi
sentences.l: Then the judges made-firm the contract of the marriage, and prayed for the two of them with the triumph and the success.
sentences.i: Then the judges sealed the marriage contract and prayed that the couple might prosper and succeed.
sentences.n: daʿā li-… bi-…, “pray for someone for something”: li- names the person, bi- what is asked. Rhymed: al-nikāḥ / al-najāḥ.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ قَامَ الْوَزِيرُ وَأَحْضَرَ مَا جَاءَ بِهِ مِنَ الْهَدَايَا وَنَفَائِسِ التُّحَفِ وَالْعَطَايَا وَقَدَّمَ الْجَمِيعَ لِلْمَلِكِ زَهْرْ شَاه
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika qāma al-wazīru wa-aḥḍara mā jāʾa bihi mina al-hadāyā wa-nafāʾisi al-tuḥafi wa-al-ʿaṭāyā wa-qaddama al-jamīʿa li-al-maliki zahrshāh
sentences.l: And at that the vizier rose and brought what he had come with of the gifts and the precious-ones of the rarities and the presents, and offered the whole to King Zahrshāh.
sentences.i: At that the vizier rose and had brought in all he had come with, the gifts, the precious rarities and the presents, and offered them all to King Zahrshāh.
sentences.n: jāʾa bi-, “come with, bring”: the verb chooses the bi-. li-, “to”. Rhymed: al-hadāyā / al-ʿaṭāyā.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الْمَلِكَ أَخَذَ فِي تَجْهِيزِ ابْنَتِهِ وَإِكْرَامِ الْوَزِيرِ وَعَمَّ بِوَلَائِمِهِ الْعَظِيمَ وَالْحَقِيرَ وَاسْتَمَرَّ فِي إِقَامَةِ الْفَرَحِ مُدَّةَ شَهْرَيْنِ وَلَمْ يَتْرُكْ فِيهِ شَيْأً مِمَّا يَسُرُّ الْقَلْبَ وَالْعَيْنَ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-malika akhadha fī tajhīzi ibnatihi wa-ikrāmi al-wazīri wa-ʿamma bi-walāʾimihi al-ʿaẓīma wa-al-ḥaqīra wa-istamarra fī iqāmati al-faraḥi muddata shahrayni wa-lam yatruk fīhi shayʾan mimmā yasurru al-qalba wa-al-ʿayna
sentences.l: Then the king set-about the equipping of his daughter and the honouring of the vizier, and covered with his banquets the great and the lowly, and continued in the holding of the festivity (for) the space of two months, and did not leave in it a thing of what gladdens the heart and the eye.
sentences.i: Then the king set about preparing his daughter's trousseau and honouring the vizier. His banquets reached great and small alike, and he kept the wedding festivities going for two months, leaving out nothing that gladdens heart and eye.
sentences.n: akhadha fī, “take to”, means to begin doing something. tajhīz is fitting out a bride with her trousseau. bi-, “with”: ʿamma bi-, “include everyone in”. Rhymed: al-wazīr / al-ḥaqīr, shahrayn / al-ʿayn.

sentences.t: وَلَمَّا تَمَّ مَا تَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ الْعَرُوسَةُ أَمَرَ الْمَلِكُ بِإِخْرَاجِ الْخِيَامِ فَضُرِبَتْ بِظَاهِرِ الْمَدِينَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-lammā tamma mā taḥtāju ilayhi al-ʿarūsatu amara al-maliku bi-ikhrāji al-khiyāmi fa-ḍuribat bi-ẓāhiri al-madīnati
sentences.l: And when was complete what the bride needs, the king commanded the bringing-out of the tents, and they were pitched at the outside of the city.
sentences.i: When everything the bride needed was ready, the king ordered the tents brought out, and they were pitched outside the city.
sentences.n: al-ʿarūsa, “the bride”, is the colloquial form of Classical al-ʿarūs. amara bi-, “command”: the verb chooses the bi-; in bi-ẓāhiri the bi- means “at”.

sentences.t: وَعَبُّوا الْقُمَاشَ فِى الصَّنَادِيقِ وَهَيَّئُوا الْجَوَارِى الرُّومِيَّاتِ وَالْوَصَائِفَ التُّرْكِيَّاتِ وَأَصْحَبَ الْعَرُوسَةَ بِنَفِيسِ الذَّخَائِرِ وَثَمِينِ الْجَوَاهِرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ʿabbū al-qumāsha fī al-ṣanādīqi wa-hayyaʾū al-jawārī al-rūmiyyāti wa-al-waṣāʾifa al-turkiyyāti wa-aṣḥaba al-ʿarūsata bi-nafīsi al-dhakhāʾiri wa-thamīni al-jawāhiri
sentences.l: And they packed the cloth in the chests, and readied the slave-girls the Greek and the maid-servants the Turkish, and he sent-along-with the bride (things) of precious of the treasures and costly of the jewels.
sentences.i: They packed the fabrics into chests and made ready the Greek slave girls and the Turkish maidservants, and the king sent with the bride the most precious of treasures and the costliest of jewels.
sentences.n: ʿabbū is Middle Arabic for Classical ʿabbaʾū, “they packed, filled”, with the hamza dropped. Rūmī means from Byzantium, the lands of the Greeks. aṣḥaba … bi-, “send someone with”: bi- names what goes along with her.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ صَنَعَ لَهَا مِحَفَّةً مِنَ الذَّهَبِ الْأَحْمَرِ مُرَصَّعَةً بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ وَأَفْرَدَ لَهَا عِشْرِينَ بِغَالًا لِلْمَسِيرِ
sentences.tr: thumma ṣanaʿa lahā miḥaffatan mina al-dhahabi al-aḥmari muraṣṣaʿatan bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari wa-afrada lahā ʿishrīna bighālan li-al-masīri
sentences.l: Then he made for her a litter of the red gold, studded with the pearl and the jewel, and set-apart for her twenty mules for the journey.
sentences.i: Then he had a litter made for her of red gold, studded with pearls and gems, and set apart twenty mules for her journey.
sentences.n: A miḥaffa is a covered litter carried between animals. “Red gold” is the stock phrase for pure gold. ʿishrīna bighālan puts the plural after the number where Classical Arabic has the singular (baghlan), a Middle Arabic habit. bi-, “with”: studded with; li-, “for”. Rhymed: al-aḥmar / al-jawhar.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتْ تِلْكَ الْمِحَفَّةُ كَأَنَّهَا مَقْصُورَةٌ مِنَ الْمَقَاصِيرِ وَصَاحِبَتُهَا كَأَنَّهَا حُورِيَّةٌ مِنَ الْحُورِ الْحِسَانِ وَخِدْرُهَا كَقَصْرٍ مِنْ قُصُورِ الْجِنَانِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārat tilka al-miḥaffatu ka-annahā maqṣūratun mina al-maqāṣīri wa-ṣāḥibatuhā ka-annahā ḥūriyyatun mina al-ḥūri al-ḥisāni wa-khidruhā ka-qaṣrin min quṣūri al-jināni
sentences.l: And that litter became as if it (were) a chamber of the chambers, and its mistress as if she (were) a houri of the houris the beautiful, and her curtained-seat like a palace of the palaces of the gardens.
sentences.i: That litter became like a private chamber, and the lady in it like one of the lovely houris, and her curtained seat like a palace of Paradise.
sentences.n: A maqṣūra is a closed-off chamber, often a woman's apartment. The khidr is the curtain that screens a woman, and the space behind it. ka-, “like”: ka-anna, “as if”; ka-qaṣrin, “like a palace”. Rhymed: al-ḥisān / al-jinān.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ رَزَمُوا الذَّخَائِرَ وَالْأَمْوَالَ وَحَمَلُوهَا عَلَى الْبِغَالِ وَالْجِمَالِ وَتَوَجَّهَ الْمَلِكُ زَهْرْ شَاه مَعَهُمْ قَدْرَ ثَلٰثَةِ فَرَاسِخَ ثُمَّ وَدَّعَ الْوَزِيرَ وَمَنْ مَعَهُ وَرَجَعَ إِلَي الْأَوْطَانِ فِي فَرَحٍ وَأَمَانٍ
sentences.tr: thumma razamū al-dhakhāʾira wa-al-amwāla wa-ḥamalūhā ʿalā al-bighāli wa-al-jimāli wa-tawajjaha al-maliku zahrshāh maʿahum qadra thalāthati farāsikha thumma waddaʿa al-wazīra wa-man maʿahu wa-rajaʿa ilā al-awṭāni fī faraḥin wa-amānin
sentences.l: Then they bundled the treasures and the wealth and loaded them on the mules and the camels; and King Zahrshāh went with them the measure of three parasangs; then he bade-farewell to the vizier and whoever (was) with him, and returned to the homelands in joy and safety.
sentences.i: Then they bundled up the treasures and goods and loaded them on the mules and camels, and King Zahrshāh rode with them for some three parasangs. Then he took leave of the vizier and his company and went back home in joy and safety.
sentences.n: A farsakh, the old Persian parasang, is about three miles. ilā is printed with a dotted ي (الي). Rhymed: al-amwāl / al-jimāl, al-awṭān / amān.

sentences.t: وَتَوَجَّهَ الْوَزِيرُ بِا بْنَةِ الْمَلِكِ وَسَارَ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَطْوِى الْمَرَاحِلَ وَالْقِفَارَ
sentences.tr: wa-tawajjaha al-wazīru bi-ibnati al-maliki wa-sāra wa-lam yazal yaṭwī al-marāḥila wa-al-qifāra
sentences.l: And the vizier set-out with the daughter of the king and journeyed, and did not cease folding-up the stages and the wastes
sentences.i: The vizier set out with the king's daughter and travelled on, stage after stage and desert after desert,
sentences.n: The print splits بابنة, “with the daughter”, across a space (با بنة). bi-, “with”: in company with. To “fold up” the stages is to cover the road quickly.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
